Two reasons why Bitcoin is crashing rn:

1) Macro - Bitcoin is not, and never has been, an inflation edge. Anyone who says that is either ignorant of its history and/or lying to you. In fact, crypto is only speculation (and crime), and therefore when credit is easy to obtain, more people gamble on it. But when things get rough (oil ~$100 a barrel, Fed not cutting rates anytime soon), crypto crashes like a rock. It did so in 2022 when the Fed began raising rates, it is doing so now…

2) MSTR - Michael Saylor’s firm has bet the farm on BTC by purchasing massive amounts of it, some ~800,000 coins. Where does it get the money? By issuing debt (such as convertible notes), preferred stock and common stock. This is is fun when the price of BTC is going up! But…

…when it starts crashing, all hell breaks lose. MSTR bought its BTC at an average price of ~$75,000 a coin. It’s now ~$60K and dropping Ike a stone. As it crashes, MSTR’s stock plummets in tandem. So now if MSTR tries to issue more debt, it will be more expensive. If it tries to sell stock, that stock will be worth less, as each new share dilutes its value. And if it were to attempt sell even a billion $ worth of its BTC (it has 10s of Bs worth on paper) a sale that large would likely blow up…
…the entire BTC market. The more investors realize the risk of MSTR going kablooey itself, the more sell the stock and the more this dynamic speeds up. Good luck to all, but one more thing…

The last time MSTR’s stock imploded, it was allegedly committing accounting fraud. The company settled the charges for $10 million https://www.nytimes.com/2000/12/15/business/microstrategy-chairman-accused-of-fraud-by-sec.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share
